$schema_note: Canonical source-of-truth for Friday loop feature-flags and their loop-closing e2e tests. The prod launch files (the rust-ws-wrapper script + the TS plist) are NOT committed to this repo, so THIS file is the authoritative, CI-enforced record of which flags exist, their intended prod state, and the committed test that drives the WHOLE loop with the flag ON. Registry gap #27 — 'every prod-ON flag has a passing loop e2e test' — is enforced against this file by scripts/ci/verify-prod-flag-tests.mjs.
why_this_exists: Recurrence prevention for the L0 silently-inert-loop disaster: three loops shipped with their flags ON in prod while NO committed test drove the loop to its outcome. A hand-proof done once is not a committed, CI-run test. The MAPPING gate (scripts/ci/verify-prod-flag-tests.mjs) runs on EVERY PR and asserts the flag<->test mapping exists + resolves. It does NOT verify the live wrapper/plist actually sets these flags — that drift check is deploy-time (see deployment_critical + the docs note).
test_execution_note: All mapped e2e_test entries are Rust friday-hub tests, RUN by `cargo test --workspace` in .github/workflows/rust-core.yml (none are #[ignore]'d; no key/network needed). Caveat: rust-core.yml is pull_request-triggered but PATH-FILTERED to rust-core/** — so the loop tests run on PRs that touch rust-core/, not on every PR. The mapped tests can only break when rust-core/ changes (and then rust-core.yml runs them), so coverage is sound; but a PR that does not touch rust-core/ gets only the existence check. A future vitest mapping would instead be run by the ci.yml `test` job.

deployment_critical.note: These flags are DEPLOYMENT-CRITICAL: their prod_state below is the contract a deploy MUST honor. A deploy must set EXACTLY the flags marked prod_state=on (no more, no less) on the named process. Wrapper-flag-durability concern: the rust-ws-wrapper and the TS plist must persist these env vars across restarts; a flag silently dropped on restart re-creates the inert-loop disaster. Drift-vs-live-wrapper (does the running process actually carry the manifest's prod_state=on set?) is a DEPLOY-TIME check, OUT OF CI SCOPE — tracked as a follow-up in docs/ops/prod-flag-test-gate.md.

coverage_legend.loop-e2e: A committed, PR-CI-run test drives the WHOLE loop with the flag's behavior ON and asserts the LOOP OUTCOME (e.g. mission born, work-item CompletedWithProof, memory becomes recallable, surface events emitted+read, clarification questions returned with zero model calls). This is the standard the gate's founding promise requires.
coverage_legend.destination-only: The DESTINATION loop this flag routes into has a real loop-e2e test (mapped here), but the flag's OWN on-ramp/routing decision is NOT exercised by any PR-CI test that closes the loop end-to-end. The mapped test is real and runs every PR, but it does not read this flag. This is a REAL coverage gap, recorded honestly — not a fabricated mapping.

test_kind_note: Rust producer tests use the program-standard split-env idiom: the env read (== "1") lives in a thin public wrapper, and the loop logic is a private *_flagged(bool) inner the test drives with the bool set ON directly (avoids cross-test env races; see the test file doc comments). Mapping to those tests is legitimate — the injected bool IS the flag's semantics. The ONLY thing those tests do not exercise is the thin env-string read in the binary (hub_agent_run_server.rs / bootstrap), which is the trivial trim()=="1" parse.

JUDGMENT: the WorkItem-status arm (work_item_status_result_for_db) shares this flag but has no by-name dispatch test of equal strength — sub-coverage gap noted in the report (the mission-lifecycle arm is the loop closure for the flag).

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the agent loop can dispatch the L2-1 `web_fetch` capability tool: the gate Allows it (read-only, no approval pause) and the CompositeToolExecutor runs an SSRF-guarded outbound HTTP fetch (host resolved + every IP validated + pinned, redirects re-validated, 512KB read / 100KB model-facing / 30s caps), returning the body to the model. With the flag OFF (the prod default) `web_fetch` is REFUSED at the gate-dispatch chokepoint (`web_fetch_disabled_flag_off`) before the executor — the tool is UNAVAILABLE and behavior is byte-identical to today. DARK: flipping it live enables outbound egress and is OPERATOR-GATED.
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap L2-1). NO real network — the mapped test stands up an in-process 127.0.0.1 mock HTTP server, drives gate_dispatch_with_policy_enforced(.., web_fetch_enabled=true) with a `web_fetch` RawToolCall against a real Hub Db + a real CompositeToolExecutor (FsToolExecutor + the SSRF-guarded WebFetchExecutor), and asserts the loop dispatches+Executes the fetch and returns the fetched body (HTTP 200 + body) in the ToolReceipt. SSRF is wired fail-closed before EVERY fetch incl. redirects: even with the flag ON, a web_fetch to a private/metadata target under the PRODUCTION SSRF policy is refused at the executor (web_fetch_flag_on_ssrf_blocks_private_target_at_executor). The flag-OFF arm (tool unavailable, executor never reached, byte-identical for other tools) is pinned by sibling lib.rs tests web_fetch_flag_off_refuses_tool_unavailable_executor_never_reached + web_fetch_flag_off_is_byte_identical_for_other_tools; the exact-'1' env matcher by web_fetch_enabled_from_only_literal_one_enables. The SSRF guard's per-range blocking (RFC1918/loopback/link-local/metadata/ULA + DNS-resolved + non-http) is table-tested in src/ssrf_guard.rs; the executor's GET/POST + 512KB read cap + 100KB truncation + timeout + HTML-to-text + redirect-revalidation in src/http_tools.rs (all mock-server, no real net).

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the agent loop can dispatch the L2 `subagent` capability tool: the running agent delegates ONE bounded sub-task to a fresh nested agent loop and gets the sub-agent's final message back. Spawning MINTS a TrustGrant whose TrustBoundaries are the INTERSECTION of the parent's grant with the requested scope (never a superset, by construction — the in-product producer that un-bricks parity-registry #7 trust mint->enforce), issued via the EXISTING friday-storage trust-issue path. The sub-agent runs the SAME gate-mandatory loop under a child RunPolicy ⊆ the parent (subagent disabled => no recursion; read-only when its grant has no mutating tool; principal inherited from the parent — no owner spoof; max_turns clamped + a count cap of 3); its model calls bill to its own derived sub-run (no double-bill). With the flag OFF (the prod default) `subagent` is REFUSED at the gate-dispatch chokepoint (`subagent_disabled_flag_off`) before classify AND the dispatch-seam interception never fires — the tool is UNAVAILABLE and hidden from the model menu, so behavior is byte-identical to today. DARK: flipping it live mints durable trust grants + spawns sub-agent loops and is OPERATOR-GATED.
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (L2 subagent + #7 trust-mint producer). NO real model/provider, NO real network — the mapped test drives run_loop_with_policy_flagged(.., subagent_enabled=true) with a metering scripted client against a real Hub Db + a real FsToolExecutor, seeding a parent TrustGrant (agent `friday`, read+write+spawn, High, workspace-scoped) via the LIVE friday_storage::grant_trust writer, then a parent that spawns a READ-ONLY-scoped sub-agent which runs read_file and returns its summary to the parent (which Finishes). Asserts the loop OUTCOME (parent Finished, the sub-agent's read tool actually Executed in the child sub-run) + the load-bearing properties: the minted child grant's boundaries ⊆ the parent's (risk_ceiling min, workspace inherited, allowed_tools = requested∩parent with `subagent` stripped, expiry = min(parent, now+SHORT_TTL)); the sub-agent CANNOT spawn (subagent absent from the minted grant AND disabled in the child policy); owner inherited (the child policy carries the parent's principal); both runs billed to their OWN run_id (no double-bill / no ledger-id collision) with the audit chain intact. The 8 mandatory security guards each have a dedicated test in the same module: guard1 flag-OFF byte-identical (menu snapshot + no-spawn dispatch) = guard1_flag_off_menu_hidden_and_no_spawn; guard2 mint ⊆ parent every dimension = guard2_minted_grant_is_subset_of_parent (+ the pure intersection tests in src/subagent.rs); guard3 depth cap by-construction + by-policy (tool_disabled_for_run at the chokepoint with the flag injected ON, NOT a flag-off skip) = guard3_depth1_subagent_spawn_is_gate_denied; guard4 count cap (the 4th spawn errors, no mint) + turns clamp = guard4_fourth_spawn_errors_and_turns_clamp; guard5 owner inherited / spoof param ignored = guard5_owner_inherited_spoof_ignored (+ subagent::owner_spoof_param_is_ignored); guard6 the mutating gate still applies to a read-only sub-agent (a write is `run_is_read_only`-denied though the parent could) = guard6_subagent_write_beyond_grant_is_denied_though_parent_could; guard7 billing metered no double-bill = guard7_subagent_billing_metered_no_double_bill; guard8 prompt-injection posture (the sub-agent's returned message reaches only the prompt, creates no new mutation path) = guard8_subagent_returned_message_creates_no_new_mutation_path. SECURITY (no-degrade): the mint is PURE + ⊆-by-construction (src/subagent.rs::mint_child_boundaries clamps every dimension DOWN, never widens; an empty parent allowlist stays DENY-ALL; a parent-lacked tool is dropped); minting requires an EXISTING active parent grant (active_grant lookup) — a parent with no grant fails the spawn CLOSED (never synthesizes a root grant), which is correct for the dark default where `friday` has no grant yet; the exact-'1' env matcher is pinned by subagent::flag_matcher_only_literal_one.

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the agent loop can dispatch the L2-4 memory-as-tool family — `memory_recall` (read the owner's CONFIRMED memory) + `memory_store` (propose an owner-scoped memory CANDIDATE). The gate Allows each (read-only: a candidate is non-durable and recallable only after explicit owner-confirm, so it base-Allows with no approval pause) and the CompositeToolExecutor's MemoryToolExecutor DELEGATES to the existing memory spine: recall via recall_confirmed -> cognition::rank_recall (recency-decay + PII redaction) -> gate_and_render_recall (per-item Context Passport gate); store via memory::record_candidate (state=Candidate). Both are keyed on the run's AUTHENTICATED principal (policy.principal_id()) — NEVER a model-supplied owner — so there is no cross-owner read/write. With the flag OFF (the prod default) both tools are REFUSED at the gate-dispatch chokepoint (`memory_tool_disabled_flag_off`) before the executor — unavailable and hidden from the model menu, so behavior is byte-identical to today. The auto-extraction (memory_extraction::extract_inline) + auto-recall (the runtime recall preamble) paths are UNCHANGED by this flag — it only ADDS explicit agent control. DARK: flipping it live exposes the owner's confirmed memory to the agent on demand and is OPERATOR-GATED.
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap L2-4 memory-as-tool, ported from the TS oracle src/agent/tools/friday-agent-memory-tools.ts memory_search+memory_store). NO model call, NO network — the mapped test drives gate_dispatch_with_policy_enforced(.., memory_tool_enabled=true) against a real Hub Db + a real CompositeToolExecutor (FsToolExecutor + WebFetchExecutor + WebSearchExecutor + VisionExecutor + the MemoryToolExecutor keyed on principal 'alice') and proves the FULL spine loop: memory_store proposes an owner-scoped CANDIDATE (non-durable, pending) -> owner-confirm via the existing memory::confirm path -> memory_recall returns it; a DIFFERENT authenticated principal (mallory) recalls NOTHING (owner-isolation, no cross-owner read); recall applies the SPINE's PII redaction (an email -> [EMAIL], proving reuse of cognition::rank_recall, not a new redactor). REUSE (no reimplementation): recall delegates to friday_storage::memory::recall_confirmed (same-principal exact-match SQL) -> cognition::rank_recall -> cognition::gate_and_render_recall; store delegates to friday_storage::memory::record_candidate (the SAME primitive auto-extraction uses). CLASSIFICATION: memory_recall is read-only; memory_store is ALSO mutating:false/Risk::ReadOnly BY DESIGN — a candidate is non-durable and the owner-confirm step is the gate (mirrors extraction recording candidates with no approval gate); classifying it mutating:true would wrongly route it to the Ed25519 approval-pause and block the agent from proposing memory under deny-all. The flag-OFF arm (both tools unavailable, executor never reached, nothing stored) is pinned by memory_tool_flag_off_refuses_tool_unavailable_executor_never_reached + memory_tool_flag_off_is_byte_identical_for_other_tools; the menu-hide byte-identical guarantee by memory_tool_flag_off_prompt_menu_is_byte_identical_no_memory_tools; the exact-'1' env matcher by memory_tool_enabled_from_only_literal_one_enables. SECURITY (no-degrade): store runs the sensitive_guard fail-closed BEFORE persisting (store_refuses_sensitive_content_never_persists), and an owner-less run refuses store + recalls nothing (store_without_owner_is_refused_and_recall_is_empty) — both in src/memory_tools.rs. The store->confirm->recall + cross-owner isolation + PII-redaction + missing-param paths are also unit-tested in src/memory_tools.rs.

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, after a flash turn 200s + bills but its reply FAILS the tool-call parse contract (the `Ok((Err(Parse), Some(flash_usage)))` trap), the live agent loop re-dispatches the SAME turn ONCE on a forced-`deepseek-v4-pro` escalation client and FINISHES on pro's answer — billed truthfully on a DISTINCT ledger row (flash leg `t{turn}:ledger` + pro leg `t{turn}:esc:ledger`: two truthful rows, never the same call billed twice). flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON AND the run driving a WorkItem that carries non-empty done_criteria, the live agent loop runs a SELF-CRITIQUE / VERIFY pass on the model's finish answer BEFORE accepting it (before completed_with_proof): a DETERMINISTIC, cheap STRUCTURAL-SUFFICIENCY check (answer_passes_done_criteria — fails on an empty/whitespace answer, or on a criterion that names an unambiguous required-artifact token, e.g. a path/filename/URL, that the answer never mentions) and — only if that fails — exactly ONE bounded self-critique RE-PROMPT to the model ('your answer does not meet <criteria>; revise', SAME finish contract) whose revised answer is then accepted (passing or not). This consumes done_criteria, which today ride every WorkItem but no engine reads. The done_criteria are loaded (one friday_storage::mission::get_work_item read) ONLY when the flag is ON and a WorkItem is bound; flag-OFF reads nothing. With the flag OFF (the prod default) the Finish arm returns the model's answer verbatim with NO deterministic check and NO extra model call — BYTE-IDENTICAL to today. DARK: flipping it live spends ONE extra metered model call per deficient finish and is OPERATOR-GATED (provider quota).
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (brainstorm (a)#2 — the canonical cheap->strong amplifier). NO real model/provider, NO real network — the mapped test drives run_loop_with_policy_flagged(.., self_critique_enabled=true, done_criteria=['produce report.md']) against a real Hub Db + a real FsToolExecutor + a CritiqueScriptedClient (a metering scripted client that bills a fixed usage per call, so the token_ledger row count is an EXACT proxy for model-calls-made), and asserts the LOOP OUTCOME: a deficient (empty) finish FAILS the deterministic check -> EXACTLY ONE self-critique re-prompt is issued (the 2nd prompt restates the criteria + the rejected answer + keeps the one-JSON-object finish contract) -> the mocked revised answer is accepted -> the run Finishes with the revised message AND exactly TWO ledger rows (one loop turn + one critique call). The reserved-sentinel id-namespace (CRITIQUE_BILL_TURN = u64::MAX) is proven STRUCTURALLY: had the critique bill reused the turn's r1:t0:ledger ids it would PK-collide and panic the test's .unwrap(); the run reaching Finished with two ledger rows IS the no-collision proof. STRICT BOUNDS (no-runaway): the pass lives in the Finish arm (the loop's single {tool:none,answer} chokepoint that RETURNS the loop), so it fires AT MOST ONCE per run; at most ONE re-prompt, after which the (possibly still-failing) revised answer is accepted unconditionally — NEVER a verify loop — pinned by self_critique_is_bounded_to_one_reprompt_revised_still_failing_is_accepted (a 3rd scripted finish is never consumed). STRUCTURAL NO-DEGRADE (scoped, honest): the flag-OFF and the no-criteria paths are BYTE-IDENTICAL (no check, no extra call, answer verbatim); and a re-prompt that ERRORS (self_critique_reprompt_error_falls_back_to_original_answer_no_degrade) or parses to a TOOL call (self_critique_reprompt_to_tool_falls_back_to_original_answer) FALLS BACK to the ORIGINAL answer and still Finishes (a critique failure can never fail the run). The SUCCESS branch returns the revised Finish unconditionally, so on a deterministic-check FALSE-FAIL (a good answer wrongly rejected) the accepted revision could differ from the original — this is inherent to the feature, NOT a global 'never worse than no-critique' guarantee; whether a revised Finish actually improves on the original is part of the operator A/B below. The flag-OFF / no-criteria byte-identical guarantee is pinned by self_critique_flag_off_is_byte_identical_no_extra_call + self_critique_no_criteria_is_byte_identical_even_when_flag_on; the criteria-LOAD half (get_work_item -> judgment_memory.done_criteria, loaded only flag-ON-with-a-bound-WorkItem, fail-safe to empty on read-error/missing-row) is pinned by done_criteria_for_critique_loads_only_when_enabled_with_a_bound_work_item; a PASSING finish makes no re-prompt by self_critique_passing_finish_makes_no_reprompt; the exact-'1' env matcher by self_critique_enabled_from_only_opt_in_enables; the deterministic check's precision (prose criteria impose no token, artifact tokens matched case-insensitively/punctuation-trimmed, empty answer always fails) by answer_passes_done_criteria_deterministic_check. The env read lives in the public run_loop_with_policy chokepoint (every production loop path funnels through it), same split-env idiom as FRIDAY_CLARIFICATION_GATE, so the injected-bool test IS the flag's semantics; the subagent child passes self_critique_enabled=false + empty criteria (a child is never the bound WorkItem). HONEST CAVEAT: whether the self-critique re-prompt MEASURABLY IMPROVES a real model's output (vs the cheap deterministic catch of empty/stub/truncated finishes it already provides) needs a real-model A/B (provider quota spend) and is NOT run here — the committed tests prove the WIRING + the structural sufficiency gate + the one-bounded-reprompt + no-degrade, NOT the semantic-quality delta. The deterministic check is a STRUCTURAL sufficiency gate, NOT a semantic verifier of done_criteria — that is the operator-gated A/B.

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the Codex authorize-only gated-turn EXECUTOR is given the operator's PUBLIC Ed25519 verify key (the runtime's already-provisioned operator_vk, the SAME one the deepseek/claude routed loop threads), so an operator-Ed25519-signed approval bound to the EXACT protected (mutating) action can upgrade the gate's RequiresApproval to Allow and Codex continues the turn (positive-authorize parity with the routed loop). With the flag OFF (the prod default) the key is WITHHELD (operator_vk threaded as None) at the executor call site, so a protected Codex action authorizes under DenyAll and Pauses — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the historical hardcoded-None. NEVER fails open: an invalid/stale signature is rejected (Errored) and a missing one Pauses; flipping the flag ON without a provisioned key is still None ⇒ fail-closed Pause.
flags.notes: HONEST destination-only mapping. This flag is the verify-key-PROVISIONING on-ramp into the Codex gated turn; it threads operator_vk through CodexTurnExecutor::run_gated_turn -> run_codex_gated_turn. The flag's OWN forward/withhold decision + the byte-identical-OFF guarantee + the matcher are proven by the on-ramp seam KATs in src/runtime.rs: codex_positive_authorize_flag_off_withholds_vk_byte_identical (flag-OFF withholds the key even when one is provisioned), codex_positive_authorize_flag_on_forwards_provisioned_vk (flag-ON forwards the SAME provisioned key), codex_positive_authorize_flag_on_without_key_stays_none_fail_closed (ON without a key is still None = no fail-open), codex_positive_authorize_seam_threads_key_into_executor (run_task_pinned end-to-end threads the DEFAULT None into the executor — probe), codex_positive_authorize_flag_on_threads_key_through_run_codex_route_turn (injects the flag-ON decision into the real run_codex_route_turn and asserts the key REACHES the executor via the probe + the loop still Finishes), codex_positive_authorize_flag_matcher_only_literal_one (exact trim=='1'). The mapped DESTINATION test (ed25519_signed_approval_continues_and_finishes) proves the authorize-and-continue closure given a Some(vk): an operator-Ed25519-signed approval upgrades RequiresApproval -> Allow -> Codex accept -> the turn Finishes (over recorded byte-streams, no live codex). Why destination-only NOT loop-e2e: the deterministic no-creds runtime tier STUBS the executor (so a flag-ON runtime test can only prove the key was THREADED, not Allow->Finish), and the destination test that proves Allow->Finish goes through the free fn and does not itself read this flag — so no single PR-CI test joins flag-ON -> authorize -> Finish end-to-end. Companion negative proofs (given Some(vk)): hmac_signed_approval_is_rejected_downgrade_defense (an HMAC-signed approval over the SAME bytes is REJECTED -> Errored, never accept — verify-only, no self-mint) and provisioned_but_unsigned_mutating_action_pauses (Some(vk) + no approval -> Pause). DARK + OPERATOR-GATED: live use also requires `codex login`, FRIDAY_CODEX_ROUTE_ENABLED, FRIDAY_CODEX_MUTATING_GATE, AND a provisioned operator verify key — this flag alone changes nothing.
